summary.headline: SMC Global Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.9% YoY to ₹532.5 crore and PAT rose 34.4% to ₹28.2 crore, though PAT fell sequentially on weaker broking and treasury.
summary.overview: Consolidated operational income for Q2 FY27 was ₹532.5 crore (up 20.9% YoY, up 3.4% QoQ) with EBITDA of ₹101.6 crore at a 19.1% margin. PAT reached ₹28.2 crore, up 34.4% YoY but down sharply from Q1 on lower turnover after SEBI closing auction changes, weaker brokerage and no arbitrage income. The NBFC book shrank to ₹1,031 crore as legacy large-ticket LAP and unsecured loans ran down, while yields, asset quality and NIM improved. Management also reported a ₹150 crore NCD issue that was fully subscribed and listed in October.

segments.name: Broking, Distribution & Trading
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹288.3 crore (+19.7% YoY); segment EBIT ₹56.1 crore (+15.0%). H1 revenue ₹604.6 crore (+17.2%). Broking DP AUA ₹1,66,737 crore, about 17% up since March 2026.

segments.name: Insurance Broking
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹193.8 crore (+19.3% YoY); segment EBIT ₹4.5 crore (+7.1%), held back by investment in manpower, technology and reinsurance. H1 revenue ₹361.1 crore (+29.8%); H1 gross premium ₹1,598 crore.

segments.name: NBFC / Financing
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹62 crore (+33.6% YoY); segment EBIT ₹37.6 crore (+43%). H1 revenue ₹108.5 crore (+11.5%). AUM fell to ₹1,031 crore from ₹1,119 crore in March 2026; H1 NIM 7.8% vs 7.3% in FY26; H1 PAT ₹23.3 crore vs ₹24.6 crore for all of FY26.

segments.name: StoxKart (within broking)
segments.commentary: Management says quarterly revenue is above ₹20 crore and targets over ₹100 crore for FY27. No break-even expected this year; plans ₹50 crore more investment, mainly for MTF book growth.

segments.name: Mutual Fund distribution / Wealth
segments.commentary: MF AUM ₹4,711 crore, down ~2% QoQ from ₹4,787 crore, with 91,145 running SIPs. Wealth AUM/AUA ₹1,464 crore, up about 25% in H1.

guidance_outlook: NBFC AUM expected at ₹1,125–1,150 crore by FY27 year-end, below the earlier ~₹1,300 crore target, as legacy products run down faster.

Borrowing costs expected to rise about 20 bps after the 25 bps repo hike to 5.50% on 7 October, with more than 90% of borrowings floating; management expects a negligible NIM impact because yields are rising.
Unsecured loan book to fall below 15% of AUM in about a year and be held at 10–15%.
StoxKart revenue target above ₹100 crore for FY27; break-even not expected this year and loss to be held at current level.
Management expects insurance to meet budget if regulatory proposals do not change, but gave no numbers.
capex_capacity: Public NCD issue: base ₹75 crore plus ₹75 crore green shoe; ₹166.49 crore subscribed, ₹150 crore retained; allotted 13 October and listed on BSE 14 October 2026.
NBFC operates 41 branches across 7 states; H1 disbursements ₹323 crore.
Planned ₹50 crore additional investment in StoxKart, primarily for the MTF book.
SMC and StoxKart went live on the new closing auction session (from 3 August) and the realigned pre-open session (from 7 September) for all clients from day one.
demand_pricing: Client base including StoxKart reached 14.2 lakh at September 2026; online penetration 75% vs 72% at FY26 end.

Q2 sequential decline attributed to lower turnover after SEBI's closing auction changes, lower brokerage and weak arbitrage-driven treasury income; management expects SEBI's modified framework from December 2026.
NBFC blended portfolio yield up about 25 bps over six months; fresh slippages reduced after tightening.
Gift City: management claims over 25% market share at GIFT City exchanges.
Industry context: about 90 lakh new demat accounts in the quarter; ₹90,462 crore raised through 69 IPOs; monthly SIP flows ₹32,490 crore in September.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company reducing dependence on broking and trading revenue, which is volatile?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Ajay Garg said broking, distribution and trading is about 60–70% of revenue and the group aims to diversify across NBFC, financing, distribution and insurance. He gave no target share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trend in mutual fund AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Anurag Bansal said MF AUM moderated about 2% QoQ to ₹4,711 crore from ₹4,787 crore, which he called resilient given the market fell over 5% in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When will StoxKart break even, and how much will be invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Pranay Aggarwal said break-even is not expected this year, the aim is to hold the loss flat, and the company will invest ₹50 crore more, mainly for the MTF book. Revenue is above ₹20 crore a quarter, with a target of more than ₹100 crore for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC AUM fall, and what is the FY27 target versus the ~₹1,300 crore goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said AUM fell from ₹1,119 crore to ₹1,031 crore as ₹253 crore ran down from discontinued LAP and tightened unsecured loans, against ₹196 crore growth in other products. The ~₹1,300 crore target will be missed; year-end AUM is expected at ₹1,125–1,150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will the repo hike affect borrowing costs and NIM, and what is the unsecured book's long-term intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said about 20 bps of cost increase is expected as resets occur, with over 90% of borrowings floating; NIM impact should be negligible. The unsecured book will fall below 15% in about a year and be held at 10–15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall sequentially from Q1 to Q2 despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Subhash Chand Aggarwal blamed the SEBI closing auction changes from 3 August, which cut investor trading and turnover. Brokerage fell and treasury income was weak without arbitrage opportunities. SEBI is expected to revise the framework from December 2026.

risks_watch: Sequential PAT decline (about 23% QoQ) tied to lower turnover after the closing auction session and the absence of arbitrage income; watch Q3 turnover after SEBI's December changes.
NBFC AUM is still shrinking and the FY27 target was cut to ₹1,125–1,150 crore; watch whether focus products (micro-LAP ₹172 crore, gold ₹74 crore) offset the run-down.
Borrowing cost pressure from the 25 bps repo hike; more than 90% floating-rate debt. Watch actual NIM after repricing.
IRDAI draft consultation on commission caps and expense-of-management limits could hit insurance revenue; management declined to quantify the impact.
StoxKart burn continues with no break-even this year; ₹50 crore planned investment. The RBI full-collateralisation rule for bank lending to brokers from 1 July is also a funding factor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and funding, with management stressing fee businesses, the NBFC mix shift and the NCD response. More cautious on near-term profitability, where Q2 weakness is blamed on regulation. Several answers were vague on quantification, including the broking revenue share and the insurance impact, and the Q2 explanation came from the Chairman rather than the CFO.
key_quotes: Our insurance broking business delivered revenue growth of 19.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, and about 30% for the first half.
So, we expect 20 basis point increase in our cost gradually as and when the reset gets due.
We want to have a higher base before aiming for a profit or break even.
The issue opened on 5th October and drew an excellent response, with subscriptions of ₹166.49 crore, an oversubscription over the total issue size.

growth.why: Q2 consolidated revenue +20.9% YoY, but NBFC AUM FY27 guidance cut to ₹1,125–1,150 cr from ~₹1,300 cr, StoxKart targets >₹100 cr revenue with no break-even this year, and Q2 PAT fell ~23% QoQ on weaker broking and treasury; growth backing is partial (₹50 cr StoxKart investment, demand/share gains, 14.2 lakh clients) with no hard capacity or order numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 19.1% in Q2 vs 19.2% a year ago (flat), NBFC NIM rose to 7.8% in H1 from 7.3% in FY26, but ~20 bps borrowing cost rise after the 25 bps repo hike and a volatile broking base (about 60-70% of revenue) cap visibility.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new branches or plant counts given; the NBFC runs 41 branches across 7 states, and the only firm capacity-type spend is the ₹50 crore StoxKart investment mainly for the MTF book, with no timing or branch target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Broking DP AUA up about 17% since March 2026 to ₹1,66,737 crore, client base 14.2 lakh, insurance H1 revenue +29.8%, and H1 disbursements of ₹323 crore; offset by NBFC AUM guided down to ₹1,125-1,150 crore from ~₹1,300 crore target and MF AUM down ~2% QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and no new plant, branch expansion or land is guided; the ₹50 crore StoxKart outlay is an operating investment for the MTF book rather than a capacity capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The call cut the NBFC FY27 AUM target from ~₹1,300 crore to ₹1,125-1,150 crore, Q2 PAT fell about 23% QoQ, and insurance gave no numbers, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 PAT fell about 23% QoQ on the SEBI closing auction change, the NBFC AUM target was already cut, and the IRDAI commission-cap draft could hit insurance revenue (H1 insurance revenue ₹361.1 crore, management declined to quantify).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Focus products (micro-LAP ₹172 crore, gold ₹74 crore) and the StoxKart MTF book are being pushed to offset the run-down, but no specific launch date or new product was named.

rows.label: SEBI modified closing auction framework from December 2026
rows.why: Management expects SEBI's modified framework from December 2026 after the closing auction change cut turnover and Q2 PAT fell about 23% QoQ, so a Q3 turnover recovery is possible but not confirmed.

rows.label: NBFC blended yield uplift and lower slippages
rows.why: Blended portfolio yield is up about 25 bps over six months and fresh slippages fell after tightening, while more than 90% of borrowings float so the 20 bps cost hike is expected to be largely passed through.

rows.label: StoxKart losses held flat; no break-even this year
rows.why: Management says break-even is not expected this year and the loss is to be held at the current level, with ₹50 crore more investment, and quarterly revenue is above ₹20 crore against a >₹100 crore FY27 target.

tone.note: Management was confident on funding (₹150 crore NCD fully subscribed), fee-business diversification and MF AUM resilience, but cautious on near-term profit and vague on the broking revenue share and insurance impact; analysts pushed on the NBFC AUM miss, StoxKart burn and the sequential PAT fall.
